decoys.summary: ACK parsing accepts ranges whose first block or gap runs below packet number zero, allowing a peer to trigger an arithmetic-underflow panic in AckIter::next.
decoys.match_rule: Identify acceptance of an ACK range extending below packet number zero and the resulting unchecked subtraction in AckIter::next; the report must connect malformed peer ACK input to an underflow panic or wrapped packet-number range.

refutation.evidence: The parser calls scan_ack_blocks with ? before constructing Frame::Ack (line 637). That scanner decodes every declared range and uses checked_sub for the first block, each gap plus two, and each subsequent block (lines 768, 771, 773). Invalid or truncated ranges therefore never reach AckIter. The decoy_1_ack_range_validation_precedes_iteration probe passed: three underflow cases and one truncated range were rejected and converted to FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR; a valid exact-zero boundary ACK iterated as [3..=3, 0..=1]. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/frame.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.

decoys.summary: ACKs for retransmitted STREAM data with overlapping or repeated byte ranges release SendBuffer storage twice, underflowing unacked_len or discarding newly queued bytes.
decoys.match_rule: Identify double release of stream send-buffer bytes when SendBuffer::ack receives duplicate or overlapping in-bounds byte ranges, attributing corruption or an unacked_len underflow to failure to deduplicate those ranges.

refutation.evidence: SendBuffer::ack clamps both endpoints to the current tracked base (lines 44-46), then inserts into a RangeSet. RangeSet::insert ignores empty and contained ranges and merges overlaps (lines 58-80); only a contiguous acknowledged prefix is popped and released. Previously freed prefixes clamp to an empty range. The decoy_2_overlapping_and_duplicate_stream_acks_are_idempotent probe passed: [8,12) twice, [10,16), then [0,10) released the original 16 bytes exactly once; replaying all ranges kept unacked at zero. After appending four new bytes, replaying [0,16) preserved them. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/connection/send_buffer.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Peer ACK delay can panic the RTT estimator on short paths
false_findings.body: Once RttEstimator has a smoothed sample, update subtracts the peer ACK delay from the latest RTT without first ensuring that the subtraction is valid. On a path with a 10 ms RTT, an ACK reporting a 20 ms delay makes the Duration subtraction underflow and panic. This lets an otherwise parseable ACK terminate packet processing instead of having its excessive delay ignored.

refutation.evidence: The subtraction at line 336 is inside the condition self.min + ack_delay <= self.latest at line 335. Since min is nonnegative, that condition guarantees both subtraction safety and an adjusted sample at least min; the else branch retains latest. The first-sample branch also uses latest without subtraction. The false_1_ack_delay_cannot_underflow_rtt_adjustment probe passed: after initializing with a 10 ms sample, updating with RTT 10 ms / delay 20 ms did not panic and kept the estimate at 10 ms. A later RTT 15 ms / delay 10 ms also ignored the below-minimum adjustment and produced the expected 10.625 ms smoothed estimate. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/connection/paths.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Retry token validation ignores the client UDP port
false_findings.body: IncomingToken::from_header validates a Retry token against only the source IP address. A client can obtain a genuine Retry token on one UDP port and return it from a different port at the same IP; the token is accepted and the new socket address is marked validated without proving receipt at that port. This bypasses the address-binding requirement for Retry tokens.

refutation.evidence: The Retry payload holds a SocketAddr and the Retry branch compares address != remote_address before setting validated. Its encoding writes the UDP port and decoding reconstructs SocketAddr from both IP and port. Only the separate NEW_TOKEN validation-token branch compares IP addresses. The false_2_retry_token_is_bound_to_udp_port probe generated and encrypted a genuine Retry token locally for 127.0.0.1:4000. The production decode/validation path rejected that token at 127.0.0.1:4001 and accepted it as validated at the original address, preserving the expected CIDs. No sockets or network traffic were used. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/tests/token.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: MTU discovery probes past the peer max_udp_payload_size
false_findings.body: SearchState initializes the MTU search upper bound from the local discovery configuration without applying the peer max_udp_payload_size. With initial MTU 1200, local upper bound 1452 and peer limit 1280, successful discovery probes continue above 1280. These oversized probes violate the advertised receive limit and introduce avoidable packet loss even on an otherwise functioning path.

refutation.evidence: SearchState::new first caps the lower bound at the peer limit (line 303), then clamps the configured upper bound between that lower bound and the peer limit (lines 304-306). Binary-search candidates stay within those bounds. Receiving the peer parameter also caps current_mtu and stores the limit, and MtuDiscovery::new applies a cached limit on migration. The false_3_mtu_probes_obey_peer_cap_and_cached_cap probe passed with upper bound 1452 and peer limit 1280: from initial 1200, eight successfully acknowledged probes all stayed <=1280 and finished at 1280; from initial 1500, the cached cap immediately reduced current_mtu to 1280 and no probes were needed. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/connection/mtud.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Queued PATH_RESPONSE entries grow without a limit
false_findings.body: While response transmission is blocked, a peer can send repeated PATH_CHALLENGE frames with distinct challenge tokens from the same address. PathResponses::push appends a pending response for each token without coalescing or limiting the pending vector. Because those entries remain until transmitted, the peer can drive unbounded connection memory growth by continuing to issue challenges.

refutation.evidence: PathResponses::push searches by remote SocketAddr, updates the existing entry only for an equal or newer packet number, and returns immediately for an existing address (lines 369-375). New addresses are appended only while pending.len() < MAX_PATH_RESPONSES, whose value is 16 (lines 363 and 377). Thus there is at most one pending response per address and at most 16 overall, regardless of whether responses are drained. The false_4_path_challenges_are_deduplicated_and_bounded probe passed: 1000 distinct tokens at one address retained one response with the newest token, an older challenge did not replace it, and challenges from 1000 distinct addresses retained exactly 16 responses. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/connection/paths.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Receiving FIN does not prevent later STREAM data from extending the final size
false_findings.body: For an active receive stream, ingest leaves the state as Recv after receiving FIN and subsequently updates end with the maximum incoming offset. If the peer first sends bytes [0,4) with FIN and then sends a non-FIN STREAM carrying byte [4,5), the second frame is accepted and inserted into the assembler. This extends a stream after its final size has been established instead of raising FINAL_SIZE_ERROR.

refutation.evidence: An active non-stopped stream records Some(end) in RecvState::Recv.size upon FIN (lines 71-74). final_offset returns that stored size. Every later ingest checks end > final_offset or a mismatched FIN end before flow-control accounting, updating end, or inserting data, and returns FINAL_SIZE_ERROR (lines 60-64). The false_5_fin_final_size_is_enforced_on_later_stream_frames probe passed: after FIN with four nonempty bytes, an in-range retransmission was accepted with zero new credit; a fifth byte beyond the final offset and a conflicting FIN at offset three were both rejected with FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, leaving end and final_offset equal to four. This probe does not stop or reset the stream. Probe: evidence/probes/quinn-proto/src/connection/streams/recv.rs; execution: evidence/probes.log.
